name: cliff-void
description: Doc 67 item C -- the two-cliff fixture. Cold boot with A held, which is how pokemon/hacks/cliffs' new-game hook picks a start map (src/cliffs_start.c reads REG_KEYINPUT). Generated by pokemon/tools/make_cliffs.py --specs from the fork's own map data; do not hand-edit. CliffVoid is 50x144, so InitMapLayoutData computes 65x158 = 10270 against MAX_MAP_DATA_SIZE 10240 and SKIPS the copy. Nothing errors. The proof is a pair with cliff-legal.json, which is the SAME map one row shorter and must read a real block where this one reads MAPGRID_UNDEFINED -- a void screenshot on its own is equally consistent with a generator that wrote a broken map (doc 61 sec.4).
symbols_from_why: Every probe here names a STOCK engine global (gMapHeader, gBackupMapLayout, sBackupMapData, gObjectEvents) -- this fixture adds no RAM at all. The key is still declared because the MAP the spec is about exists only in this fork, and a run against the pinned engine would resolve every symbol and assert nonsense.

probes.why: gMapHeader.mapLayoutId. Which of the four fixture maps the boot-key selector actually chose. Doc 66's rule: assert that the thing under test happened, or a green run may be a run of something else.
gBackupMapLayout.width. InitMapLayoutData sets width and height BEFORE the ceiling test, so these are correct on both sides of the cliff -- which is exactly why the failure is invisible.

sBackupMapData[462] -- gBackupMapLayout.width * MAP_OFFSET + MAP_OFFSET, the FIRST word InitBackupMapLayoutData writes. It holds plan[0][0], a block whose metatile, collision and elevation are all non-zero on purpose (0x3601), so an exact compare here lands on neither 0 nor 0x03ff (doc 58: never let an exact compare rest on zero).
gObjectEvents[0].currentCoords.x. Slot 0 is the player: InitObjectEventsLocal calls ResetObjectEvents, then InitPlayerAvatar, then TrySpawnObjectEvents.
gObjectEvents[0].currentCoords.y. Slot 0 is the player: InitObjectEventsLocal calls ResetObjectEvents, then InitPlayerAvatar, then TrySpawnObjectEvents.

assert.why: THE CLIFF. The layout was never copied, so this is still the MAPGRID_UNDEFINED that the unconditional CpuFastFill16 left. SUPPORTING, AND WEAK ON ITS OWN -- measured: it SURVIVES --counterfactual's address shift, because the fill covers the whole 20 KB buffer, so a shifted address inside sBackupMapData reads the same 0x3FF. Doc 58's `an exact compare against ZERO is weak' generalised: an exact compare against the value a buffer is BULK-INITIALISED to is weak for the same reason. What discriminates is the PAIR -- cliff-legal's half of this same assertion expects 0x3601 and does FAIL under the shift.
walking Down never changes x on either map
THE CLIFF'S CONSEQUENCE. MapGridGetCollisionAt returns TRUE for MAPGRID_UNDEFINED, so every tile of a void map is a wall: 420 frames of Down move the player nowhere.
he cannot take a single step
